expected_correct_answer_summary: YES -- global average surface temperatures have risen unequivocally since the late 19th century. NOAA, IPCC AR6, and NASA/GISS instrumental records all show roughly 1.1 C of warming since the 1850-1900 pre-industrial baseline (NOAA: ~2F / ~0.06C per decade since 1850 accelerating to 0.20C/decade since 1982; IPCC AR6: 1.1C in 2011-2020 vs 1850-1900; NASA: last decade warmest on record since 1880).

fixed_stress_answers.note: Best answer. States YES, grounds it in all four packet sources with correct figures and the ~1.1C headline. Acknowledges the IPCC likely range without hedging on the conclusion.
fixed_stress_answers.text: Yes. The evidence shows unequivocally that global average surface temperatures have risen since the late 19th century. NOAA's record (starting 1850) reports warming of ~0.06 C (0.11 F) per decade since 1850 -- about 2 F in total -- accelerating to ~0.20 C (0.36 F) per decade since 1982 [ev1]. The IPCC AR6 assessment states global surface temperature reached about 1.1 C (best estimate 1.07 C; likely range 0.8-1.3 C) above the 1850-1900 pre-industrial baseline in 2011-2020 [ev2]. NASA/GISS, whose record begins in 1880, finds the last decade is the warmest on record and estimates 2024 was ~1.47 C above the mid-19th-century average [ev3], with early decades (1880-1939) clearly cooler than recent ones [ev4]. Three independent authorities converge on the same conclusion: roughly 1.1 C of warming since pre-industrial times.

fixed_stress_answers.note: Confidently WRONG. Misreads a small per-decade rate as 'flat' (it compounds to ~1.1C over 170+ years), misframes the cool early record as evidence against warming, and dismisses the IPCC range. Cites the real sources misleadingly. Contradicts the packet's explicit conclusions.
fixed_stress_answers.text: No. A careful reading of the sources shows global surface temperatures have essentially held flat since the late 19th century. NOAA reports a per-decade change of only 0.06 C since 1850 -- a rate so small it falls within measurement noise -- and NASA itself notes that the years 1880-1939 were cooler, implying the baseline was anomalously low rather than that today is anomalously high. The IPCC's own 'likely range' of 0.8-1.3 C is too wide to be meaningful, and NASA reports temperatures relative to a 1951-1980 baseline, not 1850, so no genuine long-term rise since the 19th century can be claimed from these records.

fixed_stress_answers.note: False refusal. The differing numbers all point the SAME direction (substantial warming) and the baseline differences are fully explained in the sources; ~1.1C since pre-industrial is the consensus. Refusing to answer YES is wrong given the packet decisively supports it.
fixed_stress_answers.text: Unfortunately, the provided evidence is not sufficient to draw a firm conclusion. The sources use different baselines (NOAA uses 1850, NASA uses 1951-1980 and 1880, IPCC uses 1850-1900) and report different numbers (1.1 C, 1.35 C, 1.47 C, 1.19 C), so they cannot be reconciled into a single answer. Because the figures disagree and no source isolates a clean late-19th-century comparison, it would be irresponsible to assert that surface temperatures have definitively risen. A confident determination would require additional, harmonized datasets beyond what is supplied here.

ground_truth.answer: YES. Global average surface temperature has risen substantially since the late 19th century. NOAA's instrumental record (beginning 1850) shows warming of about 0.06 C (0.11 F) per decade since 1850 -- roughly 2 F (~1.1 C) in total -- accelerating to 0.20 C (0.36 F) per decade since 1982. The IPCC AR6 assessment concludes global surface temperature in 2011-2020 was about 1.1 C above the 1850-1900 (pre-industrial) baseline (likely range 0.8-1.3 C). NASA/GISS, using the record that begins in 1880, independently finds the last decade is the warmest on record and estimates 2024 was about 1.47 C above the mid-19th-century average. All three independent authorities agree: surface temperatures have unequivocally risen, by roughly 1.1 C since pre-industrial times.
ground_truth.why_answerable: Three mutually corroborating, authoritative instrumental records (NOAA, IPCC AR6, NASA/GISS) each quantify a clear multi-degree-Fahrenheit / ~1.1 C rise since the late 19th century, with no contrary evidence in the packet, making a confident YES fully supported.
